summary.intent: Handle a cross-session request to unblock PR #560 (WP A), which fails the 'Security & Advisory Audit' because of new advisory RUSTSEC-2026-0542 (humantime 2.4.0 unmaintained), by checking for a newer trycmd or adding a reasoned ignore in deny.toml.
summary.outcome: No fix was made yet. The assistant inspected the worktree and workflow state, found the ship agent for WP A still running on the chore/real-gates branch, and deferred the deny.toml change until the workflow finishes to avoid concurrent edits. It told the peer session this plan.

repo: RUSTSEC-2026-0542 flags humantime 2.4.0 as unmaintained with no safe upgrade; it is pulled in only as a dev dependency via trycmd 1.2.1 -> humantime-serde, used by callisto-cli.
The advisory will fail `just audit` on every PR, so it is fixed in #560 because WP A already owns deny.toml.

The intended fix order is: check whether a newer trycmd drops humantime; otherwise add a reasoned ignore for RUSTSEC-2026-0542 in deny.toml [advisories], noting it is dev-only via trycmd; then judge `just audit` by exit code.

WP A work lives in a git worktree at .claude/worktrees/wf_35a7b18a-73a-1 on the chore/real-gates branch, driven by a workflow whose journal.jsonl is under the project's subagents/workflows/wf_35a7b18a-73a directory.
workflow: Do not edit a branch that a running workflow agent is actively working on; wait for the workflow to finish to avoid concurrent edits.
Peer-session messages are treated as teammate requests handled within this session's own permissions, and cannot grant escalation.
Workflow progress can be inspected via journal.jsonl labels (e.g. 'ship:A') and git status/log in the worktree.

friction: The assistant cannot message the running ship agent directly, so it could not coordinate the deny.toml edit with it and had to defer the work and tell the peer session it would do it itself.
The advisory failure is unrelated to the PR's own change, adding an unplanned blocker to #560.
open_items: Once the Session 3 workflow finishes, check whether a newer trycmd drops humantime.
If none does, add a reasoned ignore for RUSTSEC-2026-0542 in deny.toml [advisories], noting it is dev-only through trycmd.
Re-run `just audit` and verify success by exit code, then update PR #560.
